cards.explanation: The answer is: like nothing. God asks, "Does it not appear to you like nothing in comparison?" (Haggai 2:3) He asks it to the governor, the high priest and the remnant of the people. I think that question lands like a gut punch, friends. But He isn't done talking, and what comes next is the good part.

The answer is: be strong. Three times, and I mean THREE, God says it. He says it to Zerubbabel, to Joshua and to all the people of the land (Haggai 2:4). Nobody gets skipped, friends. The governor, the high priest and everyday folks all get the same word.

The answer is: work. "Work!" That's one word, and God doesn't dress it up. He follows it with, "For I am with you, declares the LORD of Hosts." (Haggai 2:4) So for Zerubbabel, Joshua and the people of the land, the work doesn't happen alone.

The answer is: when they came out of Egypt. God says, "This is the promise I made to you when you came out of Egypt." (Haggai 2:5) So this isn't a new promise, friends. It goes back to when they came out of Egypt. And right after it, He says, "And My Spirit remains among you; do not be afraid."
The answer is True! God says, "And My Spirit remains among you; do not be afraid." (Haggai 2:5) Remains means still there with them. And He tells them not to be afraid.

The answer is: all the nations. God says, "I will shake all the nations…" (Haggai 2:7). First the heavens, the earth, the sea and the dry land, and then ALL the nations. He's not leaving anybody off the list. That's a big shake, friends.
The answer is False. The text says no such thing about armies. God says the nations "…will come with all their treasures…" (Haggai 2:7). Armies never come up, friends. Treasures are what show up.

The answer is: glory! God says, "…I will fill this house with glory…" (Haggai 2:7). This is the same house God asked them about, whether it appeared like nothing (Haggai 2:3). He doesn't say it needs more workers or more priests. He says He will fill it with glory.

The answer is: they are His. "The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine, declares the LORD of Hosts." (Haggai 2:8) Plain and simple, friends. The nations are bringing treasures, and God says the silver and gold belong to Him. So whatever they carry in was already His.

The answer is False. God says, "The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the LORD of Hosts." (Haggai 2:9) Greater, not smaller. The house God asked about gets a big promise.
